# fluss-go v0.2.0-beta.2

This beta continues the fluss-go v0.2 line for Apache Fluss 1.0. It adds
server-side predicate pushdown for log scanners and several robustness fixes.
It removes no exported API.

## Upgrade

- Apache Fluss 0.9.1 users must remain on fluss-go `v0.1.0-beta.11`.
- Keep the root module and any HDFS, OSS, OpenTelemetry, or S3 adapter module
  on the same `v0.2.0-beta.2` release.
- Review the [v0.2 migration guide](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.2/docs/migration-v0.2.md#upgrading-from-v020-beta1)
  and the [server-side scan filters guide](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.2/docs/data-operations.md#server-side-scan-filters)
  before rollout.

```sh
go get github.com/pletorco/fluss-go@v0.2.0-beta.2
go get github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/adapters/s3@v0.2.0-beta.2
go mod tidy
```

## Highlights

- Adds `fgo.Col`, `fgo.And`, `fgo.Or`, and `fgo.WithScanFilter`, which send a
  Fluss 1.0 predicate with the table schema ID on log fetches so the server can
  skip non-matching Arrow log batches. Fluss returns a superset of the matching
  rows, so applications must still apply the predicate. Filters are validated
  when the scanner is created and require the Arrow log format.
- Closing an upsert writer no longer waits for a pending KV backpressure delay
  of up to one minute before sending its final batches.
- Connection setup failures now report a failure to close the partial
  connection, joined to the original error.
- Writer retry execution returns an error instead of panicking when it is
  called with an unvalidated retry policy.
- Updates the AWS S3 client to 1.113.2 and the pinned Trivy release used by the
  repository security gates to v0.74.0.

The exact supported surface and live proof are documented in the
[Fluss 1.0 feature matrix](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.2/README.md#fluss-10-feature-matrix)
and [live evidence matrix](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.2/docs/live-evidence.md).

## Deliberate boundaries

Historical physical-partition routing for lake workflows is not supported in
this beta. Native Iceberg, Lance, and Paimon planning remains
application-owned. Predicate pushdown applies to log scanners only; batch and
snapshot scanners do not accept filters. This release is still a pure-Go client
and does not link or wrap the Fluss Rust core.

## Verification

The release candidate is validated with unit, golden, fuzz-smoke, race,
generation, API, documentation, security, storage-adapter, and live Fluss 1.0
checks. The live suite uses Apache Fluss 1.0.0 commit
`5c07f88e50a8ff41b0ebc214a0458e5dba60be37` and image digest
`sha256:ff461b45438033da4fd1c2556d3f978f3603bb3632fe075c2bd57388339a58cb`.

No release tag should be created until the release-preparation pull request is
approved and merged.
